caseRequirements.358: Construct the two tangent candidates at the endpoints of the diameter perpendicular to the given line. Parallel lines are distinct and have no common point: if the given line is itself a tangent, the coincident candidate is not parallel to it and must be excluded, leaving exactly one admissible tangent. caseRequirements.359: Both tangent lines perpendicular to the given line are admissible. Use the diameter on the line through the center with the same direction as the given line: when the center lies off the given line, construct its parallel through the center; when the center lies on the given line, use that line itself, rather than claiming to construct a distinct parallel through one of its points. The endpoint tangents are perpendicular to the given line in both cases.

theoryRequirements: 39 defines locus through both implications; equal distances are to supporting lines; converse assumes point inside nonstraight angle; triangle bisector concurrence included.
40 treats coincidence with segment midpoint and converse points on/off supporting line; perpendicular-bisector concurrence proof continues next page.

41 direct diameter-through-chord-midpoint assertion needs non-diameter chord qualification; otherwise midpoint is circle center and the stated perpendicular conclusion does not follow. Converse perpendicular-diameter-bisects-chord holds also for diameter chord. Point41 also proves both right-angle diameter implications and excludes diameter endpoints from the locus.

42 includes secant/tangent/disjoint configurations, tangent-radius perpendicularity, equal tangent segments and equal angles with center line, converse tangent criterion, tangent construction at a given point on circle.
43 defines tangency of segments/rays with the contact point on the segment/ray; inscribed-in-angle circle centers are on the internal bisector.
43 includes existence and uniqueness of incircle and circumcircle, with contact on actual triangle sides, plus definitions of both inverse descriptions triangle/circle.
44 includes fixed points on the axis, figures and pairs of figures, examples with zero/one/three/infinitely-many axes, and equal distances from reflected points to axis points.
45 property1 needs the coincident reflected-line case in addition to distinct parallel/intersecting lines; a line perpendicular to the axis and the axis itself map to themselves.

45 includes all reflected-point configurations in figure177б (collinear perpendicular to axis, crossing sides, parallel to axis, fixed on axis) and practical monotype/folded-paint example; retain elementary distance proof rather than merely asserting a coordinate transform.

sourceCaveats.observation: The printed direct property says a diameter through the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to that chord without excluding a chord that is itself a diameter.
sourceCaveats.mathematicalBoundary: If the chord is a diameter, its midpoint is the center and every diameter passes through it; the claimed perpendicular conclusion is false in general. The printed center/endpoints triangle proof is degenerate.
sourceCaveats.requiredTreatment: Preserve and identify the printed statement, then explicitly qualify this implication by a non-diameter chord. Do not silently present the qualification as text supplied by the source. The converse, a perpendicular diameter bisects the chord, remains valid for a diameter chord.

sourceCaveats.observation: The discussion of a line and its reflection treats parallel lines and lines intersecting on the axis; an invariant line may coincide with its reflected line.
sourceCaveats.mathematicalBoundary: The axis itself and every line perpendicular to the axis are invariant. A coincident original/image pair must not be classified as two distinct parallel lines or as having exactly one intersection.
sourceCaveats.requiredTreatment: State and illustrate the coincident case alongside the two cases discussed in the source; apply it to line-construction exercises as needed.

sourceCaveats.observation: The source asks to prove symmetry of two equal intersecting chords about the line of a diameter containing their intersection, without excluding intersection at the circle center.
sourceCaveats.mathematicalBoundary: Two distinct diameters are equal chords intersecting at the center, but an arbitrary diameter through that center need not exchange them. The given condition therefore does not imply the conclusion in this boundary case.
sourceCaveats.requiredTreatment: Keep the printed condition identifiable and explain its missing qualification. Prove the ordinary statement for intersection different from the center; for the central case state that only the appropriate bisector axes exchange the two distinct diameter chords. Do not repair the source invisibly.
